495→            // A deadlock is not possible due to these condition variables:
   496→            // suppose all threads are waiting on read dependency, and consider
   497→            // one with lowest txn_idx. It observed a dependency, so some thread
   498→            // aborted dep_idx. If that abort returned execution task, by
   499→            // minimality (lower transactions aren't waiting), that thread would
   500→            // finish execution unblock txn_idx, contradiction. Otherwise,
   501→            // execution_idx in scheduler was lower at a time when at least the
   502→            // thread that aborted dep_idx was alive, and again, since lower txns
   503→            // than txn_idx are not blocked, so the execution of dep_idx will
   504→            // eventually finish and lead to unblocking txn_idx, contradiction.
   505→            let (lock, cvar) = &*dep_condition;
   506→            let mut dep_resolved = lock.lock();
   507→            while matches!(*dep_resolved, DependencyStatus::Unresolved) {
   508→                dep_resolved = cvar.wait(dep_resolved).unwrap();
   509→            }
